amenitiesDescription:
Aman Residences Miami Beach delivers the brand's full hospitality ecosystem to a sold-out ownership group of just 22 households. The tower features a private oceanfront pool and the renowned Aman Spa, with treatment rooms, wellness programming, and an oceanfront yoga pavilion reserved for residents and their guests. Dining venues serve both the tower and the adjacent Versailles hotel, with priority access to every Aman Miami Beach facility included as standard.

White-glove service includes 24-hour concierge and valet alongside a dedicated residential management team that operates independently from the hotel to protect resident privacy. Owners may opt into Aman's hotel rental program for short-term income, and receive priority access and preferred status across Aman's global portfolio of more than 35 properties worldwide.
architectQuote: The building should feel like a breath. Every surface, every threshold, an invitation to slow down, to feel the light move, to hear the ocean without trying.

signals.title: No developer inventory — entry is the secondary market
signals.body: All 22 residences sold before delivery, so the only way into Aman Miami Beach is the secondary market — pricing set by what existing owners will accept, with no competitive new inventory coming to this address.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: This is a rare combination: a Pritzker-laureate building, an operating Aman hotel next door, and a sell-out that priced the asset at the top of the market before vertical construction even began. OKO's Miami track record, including the record-setting penthouse sales at UNA Residences in Brickell, gives the underwriting real precedent. With no developer inventory left, the only entry is the resale market, and that scarcity is the heart of the case.

investmentThesis: All 22 residences are sold. Aman Miami Beach is the brand's second urban address in the United States after Aman New York, and its first oceanfront residence in the Americas. It is developed by Vladislav Doronin's OKO Group, the team behind Brickell's UNA Residences, in partnership with Aman and Len Blavatnik's Access Industries. The 22 residences presold in 2021 at a blended average near $5,000 per square foot, a Miami Beach record at the time. The adjacent restored Versailles Hotel will host 56 hotel rooms with interiors by Jean-Michel Gathy of Denniston, anchoring hotel-backed services, an optional rental program, and the long-term brand equity of Aman's global portfolio. Suffolk is general contractor. As of August 2026 the residential tower is near topping out with glazing advancing up the lower half, while the 1940 Versailles Hotel stands within the temporary external steel bracing that retains its north, west and south facades — its interior structure was demolished floor by floor and is being rebuilt inside the preserved envelope, over two new basement levels. Residential delivery remains on track for 2027.
name: Aman Residences Miami Beach

residenceContent: 22 private homes in an 18-story tower designed by Pritzker Prize laureate Kengo Kuma, rising directly on the oceanfront sand at 3425 Collins Avenue. Residences range from expansive two-bedroom simplexes to full-floor homes and a small collection of duplex penthouses, spanning 2,500 to over 6,000 square feet. Every home is oriented toward uninterrupted Atlantic views, with oversized terraces, private elevator access, and Kuma's signature angular yet soft minimalism expressed through undulating forms, tactile Japanese-inspired materials, and a seamless interplay between interior space and the ocean beyond. Full-floor residences and duplex penthouses include private pools. Owners have access to Aman Interiors, a bespoke design service offering signature Aman furnishings to maintain aesthetic unity throughout each home.
